title: Vibration While Braking
summary: Brake vibration workflow for rotor runout, pad deposits, hub condition, and suspension checks before pricing brake work.
intro: Vibration while braking usually starts with rotor and hub inspection, but tire, bearing, and suspension looseness can make the brake pedal or steering wheel shake too.
common_sounds: Grinding, scraping, or heat smell if brake drag is present
quick_checks: Inspect rotor thickness, scoring, heat spots, and runout
Check pad wear pattern and caliper slide movement
Clean hub face and inspect wheel bearing play
Check suspension looseness if vibration is not purely brake-related
inspection_priority: Inspect rotors and pads before replacing parts
Check caliper slides and hub face rust
Verify wheel bearing or suspension play if vibration persists
confidence_cues: Hub runout can cause repeat pulsation
Brake fluid and caliper condition matter
common_causes: Pad deposits or uneven pad wear
Seized caliper slide or dragging caliper
Hub rust, wheel bearing play, or suspension looseness

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Rotor and Pad Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Use when pulsation is brake-speed related and rotor/pad inspection supports it.
checks: Measure rotor condition and runout where needed
Check hub face rust before new rotor installation

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Caliper and Chassis Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Use when dragging, uneven wear, or looseness may be causing repeat vibration.
checks: Inspect caliper slides and hose condition
Inspect control arms and steering links if shake remains

recommended_repairs.description: Primary path when rotor scoring, runout, or heat marks are confirmed.
